aboutMore: things i've been told i'm 'also' into: LAMINATION. my aunt pam teaches 4th grade and when her school got a new laminator she gave me the old one for christmas and it changed my life. i charge 25 cents a page (free if it's sad). i have laminated my library card, 3 lost cat posters, a bus schedule, and one (1) fortune cookie fortune that said 'a pleasant surprise awaits.' (it was a pencil.) i also play keyboard (casio, 61 keys, 8 notes of clair de lune) and i have a little brother, max, who is 9 and asks very good questions about vampires. ok i'm going to go laminate now ~*~

blog.title: the night i read it (a true story with a flashlight)
blog.body: my cousin jenna left her copy at our house after thanksgiving. it was on the kitchen table next to the cranberry sauce. i picked it up because the cover was black and had hands holding an apple. at 9pm my mom said lights out. at 9:01 i got the flashlight from the power outage drawer and a blanket and went under. the batteries started dying at chapter 6. i got new ones from the junk drawer at chapter 9 (i walked on the sides of my feet so the stairs wouldn't creak). at 4:50 am i finished. i just lay there. it was snowing. i said out loud to my ceiling 'oh no.' at school i told the lunch lady, mrs. rucker, the whole plot while she scooped my corn, and she gave me an extra roll. i think she understood more than she let on. i've been a different person ever since. (a person with a laminator, but we'll get to that.)

blog.title: THE LAMINATION POLICY (and pricing) (effective immediately)
blog.body: ok so a lot of people have been asking. here is the policy. 25 cents a page, front and back is 40. FREE if it's sad (lost pets, a broken heart, a test u failed but want to keep for some reason). i do not laminate: money (illegal), food (i tried a waffle, it went badly, my mom said never again), or anything that's alive. turnaround is 1 day. the machine takes 4 minutes to heat up and i won't rush it. it's like a vampire. it can't be rushed (kind of). things i've done so far: an ID card for patrick's rock (name: the rock, age: older than all of us), mrs. dunn's BACK AT 2:00 sign (she got a little teary), a lost cat flyer for a cat named Mr. Noodle (found 2 days later, he came home like he'd done nothing wrong), and the whole cafeteria menu for mrs. rucker. my cousin asked if i could laminate a sandwich. i said 'what kind' and then i said no.

blog.title: 8 notes of clair de lune (and one audience member)
blog.body: edward plays piano (canon) so for my birthday i got a casio keyboard (61 keys) (my grandma's contribution) and a library book of easy piano. i can play the first 8 notes of clair de lune. just the first 8. then my hands forget what happens. i've been stuck on note 9 for 3 weeks. my only audience is my brother max (9) who sits on the stairs in his pajamas and never says anything. last night after note 8 he said 'again.' so i did it again. and he said 'again.' 14 times. it's the only review i've ever needed. then he said 'is it supposed to stop there?' and i said 'no.' and he said 'ok but it's good.' i'm going to learn note 9 for him. i've decided it's a very sad note. (it's probably not.) (i just want to be ready.)

blog.title: rain report: delaware (a log)
blog.body: it does not rain enough in delaware. i've kept a log since june. so far: 11 rainy days, 4 'sort of' (a drizzle that couldn't commit), 1 thunderstorm (my favorite, i watched it from the porch and my dad said 'come inside' and i said 'it's cinematic' and he said 'it's lightning'). on every rainy day i go to the end of the driveway with my umbrella (black, for mood) and stand there for exactly 4 minutes. mr. okafor next door asked if i was ok. i said i was just being. he said 'ok' and came out with his own umbrella and stood there too. now he does it every time. we don't talk. he's a good neighbor. he said one thing, once: 'it's nice.' that's all. i think that's the whole twilight thing honestly. it's not even the vampire. it's the standing in it.

survey.title: ~*~ the 'what is ur aura' survey (filled out at my desk, between laminations) ~*~
qa: name:
tina. just tina. in my head edward calls me 'miss'
age:
15 and 3/4. the 3/4 matters. it's the part that's almost 16, which is when stuff happens in books
hair color:
dark brown (mahogany in my novel) (brown in real life) (it's the lighting)
fear:
the end of a book. when u close it and the room is still there
best friend:
meg. she drew me as a pale horse in a tiny cape. i said it's perfect. she said 'it's a vampire horse.' it's on my wall
what's in ur bag:
a pencil (for annotating), a yellow highlighter (plot), a pink highlighter (feelings), a bookmark, tissues, and a granola bar mr. henderson gave patrick who gave me half
biggest regret:
returning a library book before copying page 214. mrs. dunn says it's on a long hold. i believe her
do u believe in ghosts:
yes. gina played me a recording from the school auditorium. a voice says 'again from the top.' gina says it's Under Review. i say it's a ghost with notes. i'm on the ghost's side
favorite weather:
light rain. not RAIN rain. the kind where the umbrella is a choice
last thing u laminated:
a coupon for a free pizza that expired in march. a laminated coupon can't expire (it can) (but it looks great)
something nobody knows about u:
i have never seen rain on the beach. we always go in july. i'd like to see the beach in the rain just once. not a vampire. a drizzle. that's the whole dream
describe urself in one sentence:
i believe things completely, which is a talent and also homework
